claims: Artemis II astronauts are scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on Friday, April 10, 2026, at approximately 5:07 p.m. PDT (8:07 p.m. EDT).
The Orion capsule carries four astronauts.
The Orion capsule concludes a 10-day journey around the Moon.
Recovery operations are handled by the USS John P. Murtha.
Artemis II is the first crewed flight to the Moon in over 50 years.
Artemis II returns from a lunar flyby.
The Artemis II crew consists of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The USS John P. Murtha will recover the crew and the Orion capsule.
The Orion capsule will hit the atmosphere at ∼23,840 mph.
The Orion capsule will survive temperatures of 3,000∘F.
The Artemis II return will be broadcast on NASA+ and YouTube.
